statement: In automatic differentiation over a computational graph representing a calculation decomposed into intermediate sub-expressions $w_i$, the propagation of derivatives is governed by the multivariate chain rule: forward accumulation propagates derivatives as $\dot{w}_i = \sum_{j \in \{\text{predecessors of } i\}} \frac{\partial w_i}{\partial w_j} \dot{w}_j$ with seed $\dot{x} = 1$, while reverse accumulation propagates adjoints as $\bar{w}_i = \sum_{j \in \{\text{successors of } i\}} \bar{w}_j \frac{\partial w_j}{\partial w_i}$ backward with seed $\bar{y} = 1$.

symbols.meaning: intermediate variable or sub-expression at node i of the computational graph
derivative of intermediate variable w_i with respect to an independent variable x (\partial w_i / \partial x)
adjoint of intermediate variable w_i with respect to dependent variable y (\partial y / \partial w_i)
elementary partial derivative of node w_i with respect to predecessor node w_j
elementary partial derivative of successor node w_j with respect to node w_i

steps.text: Decompose a computer calculation $y = f(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ into a sequence of elementary arithmetic operations and elementary functions, labeling each sub-expression as an intermediate variable $w_i$ to form a directed computational graph from inputs to output.

In forward accumulation, fix the independent variable $x$ and compute the derivative of each sub-expression recursively by repeatedly substituting the derivative of inner functions using the chain rule: $\frac{\partial y}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial y}{\partial w_{n-1}} \frac{\partial w_{n-1}}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial y}{\partial w_{n-1}} \left(\frac{\partial w_{n-1}}{\partial w_{n-2}} \frac{\partial w_{n-2}}{\partial x}\right) = \cdots$, yielding the single-variable recursive relation $\frac{\partial w_i}{\partial x} = \frac{\partial w_i}{\partial w_{i-1}} \frac{\partial w_{i-1}}{\partial x}$.

For an intermediate variable $w_i$ that has multiple predecessors in the computational graph, apply the multivariate chain rule across all incoming edges to compute the augmented derivative: $\dot{w}_i = \sum_{j \in \{\text{predecessors of } i\}} \frac{\partial w_i}{\partial w_j} \dot{w}_j$, where $\dot{w}_i = \frac{\partial w_i}{\partial x}$ and the pass is initialized with seed $\dot{x} = 1$ and zeros for all other independent variables.

In reverse accumulation, fix the dependent variable $y$ and recursively compute the derivative with respect to each sub-expression from outside to inside using the chain rule: $\frac{\partial y}{\partial x} = \left(\left(\frac{\partial y}{\partial w_3} \frac{\partial w_3}{\partial w_2}\right) \frac{\partial w_2}{\partial w_1}\right) \frac{\partial w_1}{\partial x} = \cdots$, giving the single-variable adjoint relation $\frac{\partial y}{\partial w_i} = \frac{\partial y}{\partial w_{i+1}} \frac{\partial w_{i+1}}{\partial w_i}$.

For an intermediate variable $w_i$ that has multiple successors in the computational graph, apply the multivariate chain rule to accumulate the adjoints from all paths that depend on $w_i$: $\bar{w}_i = \sum_{j \in \{\text{successors of } i\}} \bar{w}_j \frac{\partial w_j}{\partial w_i}$, where $\bar{w}_i = \frac{\partial y}{\partial w_i}$ and the reverse traversal is initialized with seed $\bar{y} = \frac{\partial y}{\partial y} = 1$.

assumptions.assumption: The computer calculation can be decomposed into elementary arithmetic operations (+, -, *, /) and elementary functions (exp, log, sin, cos, etc.) that are differentiable.
assumptions.breaks_when: The calculation contains operations or functions whose partial derivatives are undefined or non-differentiable at the evaluation point.

assumptions.assumption: Intermediate variables and their dependencies form a directed acyclic graph structure permitting well-ordered topological forward and reverse sweeps.
assumptions.breaks_when: Evaluation dependencies contain cycles or cannot be resolved into an acyclic predecessor-successor structure.

failure_modes.mode: Memory exhaustion during reverse accumulation tape storage
failure_modes.signature: High memory consumption or out-of-memory error during execution
failure_modes.cause: Storing intermediate variables $w_i$ and the instructions producing them on a tape (Wengert list) consumes significant memory when the computational graph is very large and neither checkpointing nor rematerialization is applied.

failure_modes.mode: Computational inefficiency from suboptimal accumulation direction
failure_modes.signature: High runtime due to excessive sweep counts
failure_modes.cause: Performing forward accumulation on functions $f: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}^m$ where $n \gg m$ requires $n$ sweeps instead of $m$, or performing reverse accumulation when $n \ll m$ incurs unnecessary reverse sweeps and tape overhead.
